[[Surtling Trophy]] | health 0star = 20 | damage 0star = Fireball: 10 Blunt, 40 Fire | health 1star = 40 | damage 1star = Fireball: 15 Blunt, 60 Fire | health 2star = 60 | damage 2star = Fireball: 20 Blunt, 80 Fire | abilities = Fireball (3s) | veryweak = | weak = Frost, Water | resistant = | veryresistant = | immune = Fire, Poison, Spirit | neutral = |stagger=50%|faction=Demon}} '''Surtlings''' are aggressive [[creatures]] found near [[Fire geysers]] in [[Swamp]]s. They are small flaming imps that are relatively weak, especially in [[Swamp]]s where the constant raining significantly reduces the damage from their ranged fireball attack. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Surtlings|Aggressive creature strategies#Surtling}} Surtlings spawning near [[Fire geysers]] can be farmed through lowering the ground around the spawn area with a pickaxe. As soon as the Surtling spawns in water, it will take damage and quickly die. === Fireball === Winds back before tossing a ball of fire at the player, which applies the [[Burning]] status (10 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 40 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage). This attack has a 3-second cooldown and can be used within 10 meters of a player. The fireball travels at 11 meters per second for up to 4 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 2–20 degrees. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Coal|0star=4|1star=8|2star=16}} {{drop row|item=Surtling core| 0star=50%|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Surtling trophy|0star=5%| 1star=5%|2star=5%}}}} == Spawning == {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=3 [[spawn points]] near [[Fire geysers]]|frequency=Respawn after 5 minutes}} {{spawn row|type=During "There's a smell of sulfur in the air..." [[Events|event]] after defeating [[Bonemass]]|limit=4|frequency=6|stars=No}} }} == Notes == * Surtling is a reference to [[wikipedia:Surtr|Surtr]], also anglicized as 'Surt', a mighty giant fire jötunn in [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norse_mythology Norse mythology]. **Interestingly, in earlier versions of the game, among [[Runestone]]s the player may stumble upon in Swamp biome provided the origin of Surtlings as demonic creatures born from splintered fragments of Surtr himself after being struck down and mutilated by First Men. * The flames around 1-star Surtlings are blue, with 2-star Surtlings being pink. * Projectiles can be parried, staggering the Surtling for some time and allowing you to close the distance for melee attacks, and possibly pushing them into water. * While they take damage from water, rain does not affect them. * Before the [[Version history|Ashlands update]], Surtlings were very common and the only inhabitants of Ashlands. == Gallery == File:Valheim Surtling-1 ver0-79-10.jpg|
A normal Surtling
File:Surtling 1star.png|
A 1-star Surtling
File:Surtling 2star.png|
A 2-star Surtling
 == Lore == {{Quote|Let you who read me know of the Surtlings, that you might not fall prey to their wickedness. Long ago the great demon Surtr was brought down and destroyed by the First Men, giant warriors of whom you are but a dwindling echo. They smote long upon the body of this Surtr with swords and hammers so that his fiery substance was shattered into many small pieces. He who was made of the fire was fire in every part of him. You could not say ‘Here is the brain of Surtr’ or ‘Here is Surtr’s liver’ because every part was Surtr. So all the fragments of him were Surtr still, only much weaker in power and in thought and in memory, with no way to become whole once again. Now we call these fragments Surtlings and when they are found they should be stamped out like the last embers of a fire or doused with water to choke off their flames at the root. They will throw fire from afar and joy in causing terror and destruction. Even in his scattered dotage, the demon seeks revenge on the children of the First Men.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[ru:Суртлинг]] [[uk:Вогневик]] [[fr:Surtling]] [[cs:Surtling]] [[de:Surtling]]

They are large canines with long, bushy tails that can be bred and [[Taming|tamed]]. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Wolf fang|0star=40%| 1star=2 (80%)| 2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf meat|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf pelt|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Wolf trophy| 0star=10%|1star=10%| 2star=10%}}}} ==Spawning== {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Mountains]] during the daytime|limit=3|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the [[Mountains]] during the nighttime, despawn at dawn|limit=6|stars=Yes|frequency=5}} {{spawn row|type=From breeding|limit=4, within 10 meters|frequency=-|stars=Inherited from the parent}} {{spawn row|type=During "You are being hunted" [[Events|event]] after defeating [[Bonemass]]|limit=6|frequency=6|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Wolf Mountain]]|limit=8|frequency=4|stars=Yes}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating wolves|Aggressive creature strategies#Wolf}} === Attack === This attack has three variations, each with its own 5-second cooldown: a left-swinging bite, a right-swinging bite, and a lunging bite (70 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). In practice, this means that Wolves will typically attack three times in a quick succession before retreating for a moment. These attacks extend 2 meters out in a 60.1-degree horizontal arc and can be used within 2 meters of a player. ==Taming== ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming|Taming.]]'' Wolves can make for powerful allies, both when following a player and when roaming around the built structures. Nighttime Wolves try to despawn during the day, so the taming of starred Wolves must be started during the night. Tamed Wolves will not retaliate against players when they or other Wolves are attacked/killed. A Wolf attacked by a player will be frightened, running around the nearby area for a few seconds before returning to their normal state. Once the taming has started, they will no longer try to flee and will also eat during the day. Taming a Wolf takes 30 minutes, if given enough food. == Breeding == Wolves can breed provided the Wolf is happy and well-fed with [[Boar Meat]] or other raw meat except wolf meat, seeker meat, and bear meat, and there is another Wolf within 3 meters, and no more than 4 Wolves within 10 meters. Once these requirements are met, the Wolf will accumulate love points with each other until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy will last a minimum of 1 minute, after which the birth of the baby Wolf is random chance. Once born, the baby Wolf will take 50 minutes to mature into an adult. == Gallery == Wolf1.jpg Wolf2.jpg 1a.png|Comparison of 0, 1 and 2-star Wolves. ==Notes== *A wolf's size is affected by its star ranking. A 2-star Wolf is significantly larger than a 0-star Wolf. *Wolves can be transferred by boat by building a dock with a plank directly over the boat's deck. Wolves don't like to use staircases, so make it as flat as possible. Once the Wolf is over the boat, break the planks it is standing on to load the Wolf onto it. *Wolves will try to fight [[Serpent|Serpents]]. *Wolves will take collision damage if placed on top of the boat. Collision can occur from fish, rocks, and other unknown entities. The collision can occur at any time regardless of the boat's speed; and when it does, it will instantly kill the Wolf. This also occurs with Boars. *When roaming around an area where enemies drop meat, Wolves can not only sustain their numbers but multiply at an alarming rate. This has the advantage of keeping an area highly safe, though overpopulation can become a problem (running into players/carts, attacking structures, stutter on lower end systems, noise). *Tamed Wolves that are set to follow a player will remain where they are when the player logs out or portals beyond their detection range, regardless of the duration of the player's absence. Furthermore, tamed Wolves will resume following the player when they portal/log back in, without needing to manually set them to follow again. *Like (most/all?) creatures, Wolves have infinite stamina and will happily swim across an ocean if you sail slow enough for them to follow you. *Wolves can stand firm on steeper slopes than you can. You can use tame Wolves to your advantage when scaling steep cliffs, as you can lean on them while recovering stamina. However, in other circumstances, their eagerness to approach may nudge you into a tight corner or even off of a precipice. *When being raided by Wolves, it is not necessary to be near a structure for a raid to occur, unlike most raids. *2 Star Wolves can destroy stone structures == Lore == {{Quote|There are friends in Valheim but you must seek them amongst your enemies. Old friends, fire-kin, moon-singers. For centuries they have hunted alongside you, now you must remind them of the old covenant between your people and theirs. Flesh is their delight and must be your offering.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[fr:Loup]] [[cs:Vlk]] [[ru:Волк]] [[de:Wolf]]

They are slender, legless frost dragons with ice-blue scales and four horns. Drakes are the male offspring of their mother, [[Moder]]. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Drake trophy|0star=10%}} {{drop row|item=Freeze gland|0star=1}}|stars=0}} ==Spawning== {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=Up to 3 [[spawn points]] in [[Drake Nest]] (100 meter altitude)|frequency=0|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Middle]] of the tall [[Mountain]]s (100 meter altitude)|limit=2|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=During "A cold wind blows from the mountains" [[Events|event]] before defeating [[Moder]]|limit=3|stars=No|frequency=6}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Drake Mountain]]|limit=4|frequency=8|stars=No}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Drakes|Aggressive creature strategies#Drake}} === Spit cold === Fires three balls of ice at the player, inflicting the [[Frost (effect)|Frost]] effect (90 [[Damage types#Frost|Frost]] damage each). Each projectile travels at 15 meters per second for up to 10 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 10–20 degrees. This attack can be used within 5–15 meters of the player and has a 6-second cooldown. == Gallery == Two drakes vs 2 Vikings Valheim.jpg|Two Drakes attacking two Vikings as seen in Valheim PC Gamingshow 2020 Reveal Trailer[https://youtube.com/watch?v=oNx-9YsOpBo Valheim PC Gamingshow 2020 Reveal Trailer] A group of drakes around a ruined structure in Mountain Valheim.jpg|A group of Drakes around a ruined structure in Mountain as seen in the game's Microsoft Store and Xbox Announcement Trailer[[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vPEGKJlE9LE Valheim – Microsoft Store and Xbox Announcement Trailer]] Drake4.jpg|A Drake's frost ball attack ==Notes== *Originally introduced as a "Dragon Hatchling",[https://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-745.0-750.0 https://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-755.70-755.86] they were renamed to "Drakes" before release.https://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-477.0-477.36 Drakes are still referred to in game files as a "Hatchling". *Drakes have a maximum chase distance of 200 meters from their spawn position. After that, they will drop aggro more easily. *Players are likely to find Drakes close to a [[Dragon Egg]] protecting it. *The drops from Drakes are unusually valuable. Their [[Freeze Gland]]s, glowing blue objects dropped on death, are necessary for all frost-based weapons and foods, and their trophy is used to make the helmet for [[Wolf Armor]]. *Appearance-wise, they greatly resemble an [[wikipedia:Amphiptere|Amphiptere]], a winged, legless type of dragon, in stark contrast to Moder who resembles a huge wyvern. *Drakes may be weak to fire, however, because of the massive damage difference between [[Fire Arrow]]s and [[Obsidian Arrow]]s, Obsidian are stronger (Fire totaling 44 and Obsidian totaling 52) **This does not make their fire weakness useless, as Fire arrows make a good replacement if you do not have Obsidian arrows yet or just to save materials. == Lore == {{Quote|Let you who read me be aware of the Frost wyrms, one of the most ancient kins sprung from Ymir's body. The most common form of the wyrm are the Drakes, the small males that cares for the offspring. Most often they can be seen poised by rocky nests guarding the eggs. In contrast, the females are much larger and a rare sight to behold, but once angered they provide a vicious foe.|[[Runestone]]}} ==References== {{Creatures}} [[fr:Drac]] [[ru:Дракон]] [[cs:Drak]]

[[Lox Trophy]] | health 0star = 1000 | damage 0star = * Bite: 130 Slash * Stomp: 120 Blunt, 100 Chop, 100 Pickaxe | abilities = * Bite (4 seconds) * Stomp (12 seconds) | veryweak = | weak = Fire | resistant = Blunt, Frost, Slash | veryresistant = | immune = Spirit | stagger = 30% | faction = Plains }} '''Lox''' are aggressive [[creatures]] found in [[Plains]]. They are an enlarged fusion of both a lizard and an ox, with shaggy brown hair and reptilian skin. Lox can be [[Taming|tamed]] which allows them to be bred and [[Lox Saddle|ridden]]. === Drops === {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Lox meat|0star=4-5}} {{drop row|item=Lox pelt|0star=2}} {{drop row|item=Lox trophy|0star=10%}}|stars=0}} === Spawning === {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in [[Plains]]|limit=3|stars=No|frequency=3}} {{spawn row|type=From breeding|limit=4 within 20 meters|stars=No|frequency=-}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Plains#Alternative biomes|Lox Plains]]|limit=15|frequency=167|stars=No}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Lox|Aggressive creature strategies#Lox}} === Bite === Leans back before sweeping forward to chomp down on the player (130 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). This extends 5.5 meters in a 45-degree horizontal arc and can be used every 4 seconds when within 5 meters of a player. === Stomp === Stands on their hind legs and slams down to attack (120 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 100 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack hits in a circular area with a radius of 2.5 meters and can be used every 12 seconds when within 6 meters of a player. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming|Taming.]]'' Because Lox tend to stay in herds and wander back to the same location, it is possible to tame large groups of Lox even early in the game by periodically sprinting through the Plains and scattering the [[Cloudberries]] around places where the herds gather. Alternatively, with a decent [[Sneak (Skill)]] (and carefully watching the player's surroundings) it is possible to sneak at single Lox (or small herds) and disperse the Cloudberries this way. It is recommended to not go below 50 stamina when doing this so the player can run away if spotted. Once most or all of them are tamed, [[Deathsquito|Deathsquitos]] and [[Fuling|Fulings]] will often attack them instead of the player. With a number of tamed Lox, there will usually be one between the player and a new spawn. However, without adequate healing, some of the Lox are liable to eventually [[Death|die]] if the area is active at [[Day and Night Cycle|night]] or during certain [[Events|invasions]]. This strategy saves the player from having to build pens for the Lox, but the risk of death is high while scattering seeds. If the player's armor does not protect them from a Deathsquito attack, it may be ideal to leave everything in chests except Cloudberries and flint spears. A rudimentary [[Shelter Effect|shelter]] with a [[Portal]] in it can be used to safely enter the Plains and to keep the area active while the Lox are being tamed. == Riding == Tamed Lox can be utilized as mounts. First, create a [[Lox Saddle]], then equip it to a Lox by assigning the saddle to a hot key and using it while close to the creature. Directional keys will not cause the Lox to turn while riding. Instead, the player must move the camera, and the Lox will always move straight in the direction that the camera is facing. A Lox can move either at walking or sprinting speed - it cannot reverse. A ridden Lox is a very powerful companion. In addition to retaining their impressive health and damage resistances, a sprinting Lox is faster than even the most high sprint-level players, while also enjoying the benefit of not being slowed down by equipped armor. A ridden Lox also completely ignores a player's carried weight, able to move and even sprint while the rider is encumbered. A mounted Lox has 240 points of stamina which drain at approximately the same rate as a player's while sprinting, however, leveling the Riding [[Skills|skill]] both increases the speed of a ridden Lox as well as reducing the amount of stamina drained. It is important to note that a Lox's stamina regenerates much, much slower than a player's, one point is regained roughly every 4 seconds while the creature has been recently fed, and one every 10 seconds while it is hungry. While it is not currently possible to utilize a player's weapons while riding (trying to do so results in the player instantly dismounting as soon as the attack key is pressed) a Lox at full sprint is capable of trampling most other creatures underfoot, dealing heavy damage when it comes into contact with them. Additionally, when not making the Lox move, it will attack nearby enemies like it would do when unsaddled. == Breeding == Lox can breed provided the Lox is: * Happy and well-fed with [[Cloudberries]], [[Flax]], or [[Barley]] * There is another Lox within 8 meters * No more than 4 Lox within 20 meters * Not already pregnant * Within approximately 64 meters of a player Additionally, in order for a Lox to be able to pathfind to and eat food, it can't be in a room with a ceiling that is too low. On flat ground, 8 meters of vertical clearance should be enough, but it is recommended to have 10 meters or more if you intend to house your Lox indoors. Once met, the Lox will accumulate love points with each other until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy will last a minimum of two minutes, after which the birth of the baby Lox is random chance. Once born, the baby Lox will take 1 hour and 40 minutes to mature into an adult. == Gallery == Lox1.jpg Lox2.jpg Lox3.jpg Lox faceoff.jpg|By the time it realized it had to go around the ditch, not over, it was full of arrows. Lox in ditch.jpg|Tried to charge the ditch and smash it, but got stuck and died. File:LoxCalf.png == Notes == * The name 'Lox' is a fusion of the words 'lizard' and 'ox', which reflects their design. * The trader, [[Haldor]], has a tamed Lox named [[Halstein]] that can be found in his camp. [[Hildir]] has two tamed Lox named [[Blåbär]] and [[Hallon]]. * Approaching a wild Lox will always frighten it and cause it to become aggressive to the player. * Lox can project their melee damage a considerable distance forward by rearing up and smashing down with their front hooves. When digging ditches to block them, this must be kept in mind; a Lox does not have to be able to cross a narrow ditch to destroy structures on the other side. * [[Lox Meat]] is very healthy and a good basic HP [[food]]. [[Lox Meat Pie]] has nearly the same health and stamina gain as [[Serpent Stew]], which were the best overall health foods until the [[Mistlands]] release. One advantage Lox-based food has over Serpent-based food is accessibility: Lox can be tamed and bred, whereas Serpents must be found. {{Creatures}} [[Category:Aggressive creatures]] [[fr:Lox]] [[ru:Быкоящер]] [[de:Lox]] [[cs:Lox]]

They resemble small, goblin-like beings that appear to possess their own tribalistic culture. It is implied through [[Runestone]]s and [[Fuling Totem|totems]] that they worship [[Yagluth]], a long dead king. Fulings appear 33% of the time as club variants, 17% of the time as spear variants, 33% of the time as sword variants and 17% of the time as torch variants. All Fulings spawn with one piece of armor each providing 60 armor value and having an equal 25% chance of appearing: helmet, armband, shoulders, and legband. Additionally, they have a 33% chance to spawn with a [[Wood Shield]] identical to the one players can craft. They do not drop equipment on death. === Drops === {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Black metal scrap|0star=1||1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Coins|0star=5-9 (25%)|1star=10-18 (50%)|2star=20-36}} {{drop row|item=Fuling trophy|0star=10%|1star=10%|2star=10%}}}} === Spawning === {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in [[Plains]] during the daytime|limit=2|frequency=3}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in [[Plains]] during the nighttime, despawn at dawn|limit=5|frequency=5}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in most biomes during the nighttime after [[Yagluth]] has been defeated, despawn at dawn|limit=3|frequency=3|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=Common [[Spawn points|spawn point]] in [[Fuling Village]]s, [[Fuling Outpost]]s and [[Fuling Ruin]]s |frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=During "The horde is attacking!" [[Events|event]]|limit=8|frequency=6|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=During "They were bros, man." [[Events|event]]|limit=8|frequency=6|stars=Yes (Minimum 1 Star)}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Plains#Alternative biomes|Goblin Plains]]|limit=5|frequency=3|stars=Yes}}}} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Fulings|Aggressive creature strategies#Fuling}} Besides the spear, which can only be thrown, each weapon arcs horizontally by 90 degrees and extends 2.4 meters out. === Club === Does 85 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] damage. This attack has a 2-second cooldown and can be used within 1.6 meters of a player. === Spear === Throws a spear at the player, which does not need to be retrieved for Fulings to attack again (85 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]] damage). The spear travels at 20 meters per second for up to 10 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 4–20 degrees. This has a 4-second cooldown and can be used within 14 meters of a player. === Sword === Does 85 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage. This attack has a 2-second cooldown and can be used within 1.6 meters of a player. === Torch === Does 45 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 45 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage, which applies the [[Burning]] status. This attack has a 2-second cooldown and can be used within 1.6 meters of a player. == Gallery == Fuling1.jpg Fulingcamp2.jpg Fulingcamp3.jpg Fulingcamp4.jpg 20210330133509 2.jpg == Notes == * Fulings have unusually sharp hearing and will be able to detect the player from a much longer distance than other enemies. Chopping down trees or mining ore is likely to attract their attention. * Fulings are relatively noisy. The distinctive sound of their chatter or laughter will often be the first sign that they are active in an area. * Fulings are extremely fast and agile, but they sometimes fail to register the edge of a player-dug ditch until it is too late to avoid falling in. * Fulings are particularly slow swimmers. Adventurers may use this to their advantage, for instance, by jumping over a river (natural or player-made) while firing arrows at their now slow targets. * While most creatures in Valheim take inspiration from counterparts in Norse mythology, the Fuling seem to be an exception. The closest parallel would be the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goblin#European_folklore_and_collected_folk_stories Goblin], more traditionally used in fantasy works since their popularization within the ''Dungeons & Dragons'' setting. This is further indicated by them being named "Goblin" in the game files. * "Fuling" can be roughly translated into "ugly one" in modern Swedish. * == Lore == {{Quote|Here on the plains you will find the dwellings of the Fuling, that ancient race who once built towers and cities to rival those of men until Oden punished them for their pride. He trampled the Fuling armies, their armour cracking like snail shells beneath his feet, and tore down their cities. Only Yagluth, the great sorcerer, would not bend or break before his fury. So Oden tore his body in half and cast the remains into Valheim, where he bled into the earth and crumbled to dust, wept over by the last of his people. Now the Fuling rule over the plains of Valheim, savage and wild with only hatred and fear in their hearts. But Yagluth is with them still, an unseen force that the Fuling shamans draw upon for their crooked magic, growing again in strength as his people spread across the world...|[[Runestone]]}} The runestone describes [[Oden]] punishing the Fuling as a whole people for their pride, trampling their armies and tearing down their cities, and its portrayal of the surviving Fuling is racially motivated: it stereotypes the entire race as "savage and wild with only hatred and fear in their hearts".In-game text, Plains runestone ($lore_plains_random11). == References == {{Creatures}} [[de:Fuling]] [[ru:Фулинг]] [[fr:Gobelin]]

'''Bonemass''' is the third [[Creatures#Bosses|boss]]. He appears as a gigantic humanoid mass comprised of toxic ooze, mud and skeletal remains, likely absorbed from nearby tombs situated close to his altar.

== Summoning ==
[[File:BonemassAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|Bonemass' Forsaken Altar.]]
Bonemass' [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in [[Swamp]]s. His location can be found when visiting [[Sunken Crypts]] and sometimes ruined structures, where a [[Runestone#Vegvisir|Vegvisir]] will reveal his nearest summoning location on the map.

He is summoned by placing 10 {{Item Link|Withered Bone}}s in his Forsaken altar in Swamps. Like all bosses, Bonemass can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met.

== Attacks and abilities ==
{{For|strategies for defeating Bonemass|Boss strategies#Bonemass}}
Bonemass has an environment aura that forces raining, which means pulling him from the area cannot be used to remove [[Wet Effect|Wet]].

=== Area of effect ===
Bonemass will charge up with a thick green cloud before vomiting a wave of poisonous ooze, inflicting the [[Poison]] status on everything in a 9-meter radius around him (130 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage). This is signaled when he leans backwards. The poison cloud persists for 15 seconds and will continuously refresh the poison duration on any player that stays inside. This effect cannot be dodged or blocked. Bonemass can use this ability when a player is within 15 meters, and it has a cooldown of 30 seconds. The cloud is centered on the impact point of Bonemass's vomit; due to the size of his collision box, this results in the cloud not reaching very far behind him which gives players a safe area to retreat to that is still within range to strike him.

=== Punch ===
A close-range swipe at a player dealing up to 80 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 50 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage to players, in addition to 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage to any trees or rocks hit. This attack can be used every 7 seconds when a player is within 8 meters. It hits in a horizontal 8.5-meter 66.1-degree arc in front of Bonemass.

=== Throw ===
At 50-second intervals, Bonemass will reach into his armpit to throw out a glob of goop in the general direction of the player at an initial velocity of 20 meters per second with a spread of 5–20 degrees. On impact, this ability will attempt to spawn four random monsters ([[Skeleton]]s and/or [[Blob]]s, with equal chances for both). A maximum of eight summons of each type can be active at once; but the selection of enemies each spawning instance is still random regardless of the status of spawn caps, meaning reaching the spawn cap for one type of summon will not force spawns for the other. Bonemass will still attempt to summon creatures even if both spawn caps are reached. This ability can only be used when a player is within 30 meters.

== Aftermath ==
Defeating Bonemass provides the player with a Wishbone, which allows the player to easily locate [[Silver Vein]]s beneath the surface of [[Mountain]] biomes (as well as buried [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s in Swamp biomes, and other miscellaneous buried treasures in certain locations).

=== Forsaken power ===
Mounting Bonemass' trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds:

* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Blunt
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Slash
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Pierce
* Block stamina usage: -100%
* Block stamina return: +5

See [[Forsaken_power#Bonemass Power|Bonemass' power]] for more details.

=== Events ===
Defeating Bonemass affects the following [[events]] for that world:

* Disables: Draugr and Skeleton "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: Blobs and Oozers "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: "A skeleton surprise!"
* Enables: "A cold wind blows from the mountains." (if [[Moder]] has not been defeated)
* Enables: "There's a smell of sulfur in the air." (if a [[Surtling]] has died)
* Enables: "You are being hunted."
* Enables: "You stirred the cauldron." (if a [[Bat]] has died)
* Enables: "You feel a chill down your spine..."
Note: Two of these events unlock flying enemies that will be uninhibited by base walls and will attack tame animals. For example, bats will quickly wipe out any outdoor tame Boars (if the player has them), most likely before the player can swat them all. Therefore, in order to protect any rare animals (such as a 2-star [[Boar]]), it is advisable to build a secure indoor barn area before undertaking Bonemass.

=== Creature spawning ===
Defeating Bonemass unlocks [[Skeleton]]s to spawn at night in the Meadows, Black Forest, Swamp (additional), Mountain and Plains. They can only have 0 stars.

'''Forsaken powers''' are unlocked by defeating each boss and hanging their trophy on the [[Sacrificial Stones]]. By default, the player's set forsaken power is activated by [[Controls|pressing F]]. Only one forsaken power can be set at a time, which is changed out at the Sacrificial Stones.

All forsaken powers have a duration of 5 minutes. They also share the same 20-minute cooldown, which does not reset or reduce even when the player logs off, changes their active forsaken power, or sleeps.  

Activating a power locks the player into an animation for a couple of seconds. The player is unable to move or perform any action (with the exception of equipping or unequipping tools/weapons). 

When activating a forsaken power, all players within 10 meters will also receive the benefit of the forsaken power activated. Thus, a party of four players can keep a forsaken power activated virtually indefinitely by consecutively using each player's forsaken power. 

==[[Eikthyr]] Power==
{{Quote|The grace of the mighty stag flows through you. Your ability to move around is improved, be it on land or in water.}}
60% reduced [[stamina]] usage for running, jumping, and swimming.

==[[The Elder]] Power==
{{Quote|The power of the forest invigorates you. You shall gather its bounties faster, just as you shall regain your own vitality should you lose it.}}
+60% [[Chop]] and [[Pickaxe]] damage increase, +30% health regeneration increase.

==[[Bonemass]] Power==
{{Quote|The mass takes the brunt of your blows. The effort required to raise your shield lessens, and you can withstand harder hits.}}
[[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] (-25%) VS pierce, slash, and blunt damage, -100% [[block]] stamina cost, +5 stamina returned per block.

==[[Moder]] Power==
{{Quote|The dragon's wings urge you on. You shall always have tailwind while sailing, and you shall swiftly carry heavy burdens, even over the coldest mountains.}}
Always tailwind when sailing, +300.0 increased [[carry weight]], +10% increased movement speed, [[Resistance|Resistant]] (-50%) vs frost.

===Notes===
*This power changes the [[wind]] direction while sailing, but not wind intensity. A calm wind will not aid in travel as much as a fast wind.
*The wind direction is only changed while steering the ship. While not in control of a ship, the wind will remain at its regular angle.
*The wind change is local to each player carrying the buff and does not affect each other's wind direction.
*This power is best saved for when there is headwind since crosswind (perpendicular to travel direction) and tailwind are about equally good for sailing.
*This power will not affect the wind if you are too close to the [[World Edge|World's Edge]].

==[[Yagluth]] Power==
{{Quote|The fallen king lends you his might. A king must have the power to vanquish his foes, just as he must be able to support his people.}}
Resistant (-50%) vs lightning, +25 [[Farming (skill)]], and +10% increased damage.

==[[The Queen|The Queen's]] Power==
{{Quote|Her Majesty blesses you. In her shadow both stealth and magic may flourish, and no poison shall harm you.}}
+100% [[Eitr]] regeneration increase, -100% [[sneak]] stamina usage, and resistant (-50%) vs poison.

== [[Fader]] Power ==
{{Quote|The Emerald Flame never relents. You shall stand your ground, even when it is aflame, and you shall use all the advantages the battle may offer you.}}
+100% [[Adrenaline]] increase, 50% reduced [[stagger]] meter modifier, and resistant (-50%) vs fire.

==Notes==
* Bonemass Power damage resistance does ''not'' stack with [[Crystal Heart]].
* [[Kall Fimbulbringer]] does not provide a Forsaken Power upon hanging his trophy on the Sacrificial Stones, as doing so ends the game instead.

{{infobox character | name = Dvergr | image = Dvergr (race).png | imagecaption = | caption = | id = | aliases = | affiliation = | marital = | birthDate = | birthPlace = | deathDate = | deathPlace = | species = Dvergr | gender = | height = | weight = | eyes = Light blue, purple }} A '''Dvergr''' is a type of both passive and aggressive [[Creatures|creature]] found primarily in the [[Mistlands]]. The Dvergr are an intelligent race that resemble short, blue humanoids with glowing eyes ranging from blue to purple, and long white beards and braids. The Dvergr living in the [[Ashlands]], are red haired and of a different clan than those from the Mistlands. == Biography == Dvergr are unique creatures in that they are passive to the player unless attacked. They demonstrate both ingenuity and magical abilities, which allows them to construct elaborate structures. At some unknown point in time prior to the player's arrival, the Dvergr sealed away [[The Queen]] and scattered the key fragments to unlock the [[Infested Citadel]] across the world. === Members === * [[Haldor]] * [[Hildir]] * [[Dvergr Rogue]] * [[Dvergr Mage]] * [[Ashlands Dvergr]] == Relations with other races == === Behavior === All Dvergr ([[Dvergr Rogue]], [[Dvergr Mage]], [[Ashlands Dvergr]] and [[Imprisoned Dvergr]]) belong to the Dvergr faction. Players and the Dvergr faction are not enemies by default. A Dvergr only becomes hostile to players once it is aggravated: when a player deals damage to a Dvergr, every creature within 20 meters that can be aggravated turns hostile, and a Dvergr also turns hostile after a player damages objects inside its [[Ward]]'s area more than five times, or destroys one. An aggravated Dvergr stays hostile. [[Taming|Tamed]] creatures are not attacked by a Dvergr unless that Dvergr is aggravated.Game code: BaseAI.IsEnemy, Character.RPC_Damage, BaseAI.AggravateAllInArea and MonsterAI.OnPrivateAreaAttacked. Toward other creatures, the Dvergr follow the same rule as most creature factions: they are hostile to every other faction except [[Hare]]s and bosses, and those factions are hostile to them in return. This includes [[Greydwarf|Greydwarfs]] and [[Troll]]s, [[Fuling]]s, [[Seeker]]s, the undead, the [[Charred Warrior|Charred]] and the [[Krigen]] and [[Hexen]] of the [[Deep North]].Game code: BaseAI.IsEnemy. === In-game text === The in-game text portrays the Dvergr as insular but racially motivated: they keep to themselves unless provoked, yet condemn the [[Seeker]]s as a species and hurl racial slurs at humans once aggravated. A [[Runestone]] in the [[Mistlands]] reads: {{Quote|The Dvergr are the descendants of the great smiths of old, delvers in the deep earth, seekers of hidden treasure. Here in Valheim they mine the bones of the Jotunn and distill eitr, the stuff of magic. If left alone, they are happy with their own plans and care little for the lives of others, but when raised they will defend themselves.}}In-game text, Mistlands runestone ($lore_mistlands_random04). [[Hugin]] says: "Kra-kraaa! Stubborn fools! The Dvergr will tolerate strangers and vagrants but they are quick to anger should you upset them... Which I am sure you will manage to do sooner or later."In-game text, Hugin: Dvergr ($tutorial_dvergr_text). [[Munin]] calls them "the forlorn Dvergr clans, long since separated from their kin in Nidavellir".In-game text, Munin: Dvergr ($lore_dvergr_text). A Mistlands runestone left by Ulf is racially motivated: it stereotypes the Dvergr as a whole race as humorless "short ones" whose only cure for insult is killing: "Heed the words of Ulf and do not take the hats of the short ones from their heads. They have no sense of a jest and the only cure for insulting them is to kill them. Also, their hats do not fit common heads."In-game text, Mistlands runestone ($lore_mistlands_random06). ==== Humans ==== The Dvergr address the player as "Norseman" or "human". Most of these lines are curious rather than hostile: "Do all humans look like you? You're so... Nevermind."In-game dialogue, Dvergr Rogue ($npc_dvergrrogue_random_talk4). and "It must be strange, being human. Imagine having to crawl through small spaces!"In-game dialogue, Dvergr Mage ($npc_dvergrmage_random_talk9). When a player touches their property, they warn: "We were here first!"In-game dialogue, Dvergr Rogue ($npc_dvergrrogue_random_private_area_alarm3). and "We're only good hosts as long as you're a good guest."In-game dialogue, Dvergr Mage ($npc_dvergrmage_random_private_area_alarm4). Their slurs toward humans are likewise aimed at the player's race rather than the player's actions, though they are only said once a Dvergr has become aggravated: "Kill the Norseman!"In-game dialogue, Dvergr Rogue ($npc_dvergrrogue_random_aggravated2). and "Human scum!"In-game dialogue, Dvergr Mage ($npc_dvergrmage_random_aggravated8).Game code: NpcTalk.OnBecameAggravated plays the aggravated lines. [[Haldor]] says "I've met your kind before."In-game dialogue, Haldor ($npc_haldor_random_talk3). ==== Seekers ==== The Dvergr's hostility toward the [[Seeker]]s is racially motivated. Rather than objecting to individual Seekers, they condemn the species as a whole, wishing that they would "all just shrivel up and die" and calling them "pests" that have overrun their old mines: * "Blasted seekers! I wish they'd all just shrivel up and die."In-game dialogue, Dvergr Rogue ($npc_dvergrrogue_random_talk7). * "Damned seekers smashed our black cores! Back into the deep then, I guess..."In-game dialogue, Dvergr Rogue ($npc_dvergrrogue_random_talk_in_faction_base8). * "Those seekers are not to be messed with..."In-game dialogue, Dvergr Mage ($npc_dvergrmage_random_talk4). * "These pests have spread further than I feared. At this rate, all our old mines will be overtaken."In-game dialogue, Dvergr Mage ($npc_dvergrmage_random_talk8). ==== Giants ==== An [[Imprisoned Dvergr]] may say "Slay all the giantkind you can!" as the player leaves.In-game dialogue, Imprisoned Dvergr ($npc_dvergr_deepnorth_random_goodbye3). ==== Charred ==== The [[Ashlands Dvergr]] speak of the [[Charred Warrior|Charred]] as a group: "Those undead bastards sure hoard some pretty gemstones..."In-game dialogue, Ashlands Dvergr ($npc_dvergr_ashlands_random_talk15). and "We sure hit those charred hard yesterday, didn't we?"In-game dialogue, Ashlands Dvergr ($npc_dvergr_ashlands_random_talk_in_faction_base8). ==== Between clans ==== The [[Ashlands Dvergr]] call themselves Redbeards and boast about another clan, the Whitebeards: * "Ha! A Whitebeard would never dare to venture here."In-game dialogue, Ashlands Dvergr ($npc_dvergr_ashlands_random_talk18). * "The Whitebeards could never withstand this heat. They just don't have the stones for it!"In-game dialogue, Ashlands Dvergr ($npc_dvergr_ashlands_random_talk19). * "I could never remain stationed at just one excavation for months. Us Redbeards are meant to explore!"In-game dialogue, Ashlands Dvergr ($npc_dvergr_ashlands_random_talk_in_faction_base18). * "The Whitebeards will be jealous when they hear of our success, I'm sure!"In-game dialogue, Ashlands Dvergr ($npc_dvergr_ashlands_random_talk_in_faction_base19). == Location == Most Dvergr are only encountered in the Mistlands, where they can often be found inhabiting structures they have built out of [[Black Marble|marble]], [[copper]], and [[wood]]. Many of their structures and encampments are protected by [[Ward]]s, and damaging these structures or their contents (including any Dvergr inside or around them) makes all Dvergr in the immediate vicinity aggressive. In addition to these initial spawns, Dvergr can spawn throughout the biome in groups of 1–2. Merchants [[Haldor]] and [[Hildir]] can each be found once per world, in the [[Black Forest]] and [[Meadows]] respectively. They cannot be angered or damaged, nor can they each move from their set piece. They pay for [[valuables]] with coins. Haldor's stock expands as more Forsaken are sacrificed, Hildir's as her chests are retrieved and returned. Both the fire mages and the ice mage share a melee attack. ==== Melee ==== Pokes the player with the hilt of their staff (70 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] damage). This is accessible every 4 seconds when within 0.5-2.5 meters of a player. Despite being a straight thrust, this attack hits a horizontal arc 2.5 meters long and 90 degrees across. ===Fire mages=== Fire mages wear a red robe lined with gold and carry a pronged, fiery-red staff. They have two unique attacks: ==== Fireball ==== Brings their staff around and then sweeps down to launch a single fireball that inflicts the [[Burning]] status (130 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage). The fireball travels at 15 meters per second for up to 10 seconds before despawning. It is generated with a spread of 1–10 degrees. This attack can be used every 6 seconds when within a 1–15 meters of a player. If it hits the ground instead of a player, it creates a 6-meter radius circular blast that expands outward (100 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage). ==== Clusterbomb ==== Waves their staff for a few seconds before raising it up higher to launch a shower of nine fireballs in various directions that inflict the [[Burning]] status (100 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage each). Each fireball travels at 11 meters per second for up to 10 seconds before despawning. They originate from a point 2.5 meters off the ground and have a spread of 40–50 degrees. This attack can be used every 35 seconds when within 5–30 meters of a player. On impact with the ground, these fireballs create 3-meter radius circular fields of fire (100 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage). ===Ice mages=== Ice mages wear a blue robe lined with silver and carry a staff tipped with a glowing blue ice shard. They have two unique attacks: ==== Icebolt ==== Stabs forward with their staff to launch three balls of ice at the player which inflict the [[Frost]] status (200 [[Damage types#Frost|Frost]] damage). Each ball of ice travels at 15 meters per second for up to 4 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 8–15 degrees. This attack can be used every 6 seconds when within 1–15 meters of a player. ==== Nova ==== Slams their staff down to create an outward expanding circle with a radius of 5 meters, which inflicts the [[Frost]] status (150 [[Damage types#Frost|Frost]] damage). This attack can be used very 7 seconds when within 0–7 meters of a player. ===Support mages=== Support mages wear a yellow-and-brown robe lined with gold and carry a staff tipped with a [[Dvergr Lantern]]. They have three unique abilities: ==== Buff ==== Lifts their staff up before slamming it into the ground to apply the [[Dvergr power]] status to themselves and allies within 8 meters for 20 seconds (+20% to all [[Skills]]). This ability can be used every 45 seconds when within 1–15 meters of an ally. ==== Heal ==== Draws a half-circle on the ground before lifting their staff in the air to apply the [[Dvergr heal]] status to themselves and allies within 4.32 meters for 4 seconds (400 health ticking every 0.5 seconds). This ability can be used every 10 seconds when within 1–15 meters of an ally. ==== Mistile ==== Smashes the ground with their staff to create 1–3 [[Mistile|Mistiles]] within a 3-meter radius around the caster; a max of nine can be active at once. These orbs have 1 health and track the player to deal damage on impact (150 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] damage). These can be summoned every 35 seconds when within 1–15 meters from a player.
